text:
sara: Heads up — trying to spin up a 'fastpath' GPU spot node pool in us-west4 for low-latency burst inference. Two blockers: 1) Cloud NAT external IP quota for egress (we need sticky IPs for ACLs) and 2) 30s spot-preemption notice feels too short to flush in-memory KV cache to S3. anyone fought this combo?
ben: oof. for egress, can we use a single NAT with multiple IPs + hairpin? otherwise egress-proxy (nginx/egress-gateway) with one static IP works. for preemption: use a node termination handler + PodDisruptionBudget + fast offload. 30s is tight but doable with concurrent flush + background checkpointing.
lisa: can we avoid sticky external IPs entirely? maybe use internal-only and route through an app-level proxy in VPC with static IP. that isolates quota to 1 reserved IP.
sara: we can't change the consumer ACLs (enterprise customers) — they require allowlist by IP. so static IP per pool preferred.
kai: cost tradeoff: spots save ~60% but if we overprovision static IPs and NATs the quota/price might negate savings. consider a small reserved baseline pool for 24/7 and ephemeral 'fastpath-spot' for bursts. autoscaler config should scale the spot pool aggressively.
ben: autoscaler tips: set cluster-autoscaler expander to least-waste and use nodegroup labels like "burst=true" so we can prioritize packing. set max-surge for the rollout to avoid mass-evictions. also tune scaleDownDelay to keep nodes around for minutes to handle short bursts.
arnold-sre: re: 30s notice — for GCP preemptible, we get a 30s SIGTERM? If using spot VMs on AWS you get 2-min IMDS notice sometimes. Important to test the exact interruption hook. We run a termination-handler daemonset that catches the signal and posts to a central controller which returns a node cordon + drain request.
sara: can you paste our termination handler snippet?
arnold-sre: sure — minimal example we run in a DS: ```#!/bin/sh
# runs on node, watches metadata for termination
while true; do
  if curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/spot/instance-action | grep -q Terminate; then
    kubectl cordon $(hostname)
    kubectl drain $(hostname) --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=20
    # trigger cache-upload
    curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7777/flush-cache
  fi
  sleep 5
done
```
ben: Couple notes: 1) set pod terminationGracePeriodSeconds lower than app's internal flush timeout so the daemon can still run the flush endpoint, 2) use preemptible lifecycle probe to start background checkpoints every N seconds to reduce flush time on termination.
lisa: on NAT quota — file a quota increase to GCP with justification: "burst GPU pool needs static egress IPs for customer allowlist; propose 3 new IPs for us-west4 for QPS < 2k." Should include projected QPS and retention window.
kai: also consider using a NATless pattern: egress through a small set of proxy VMs (non-gpu) that hold the static IP(s). Advantages: fewer IPs, cheaper since proxies are small CPUs, and GPU nodes don't need public egress. downside: extra hop adds ~5-10ms.
sara: 5-10ms is acceptable for many customers, but fastpath targets sub-50ms tail. need to run perf test.
ben: if we keep the proxy pattern, add a health-check path and an internal load-balancer. implement sticky sessions by source CIDR to keep connection churn low.
arnold-sre: ops checklist I suggest: 1) request Cloud NAT external IP quota (list of IPs), 2) add termination-handler DS + pre-checkpointing library to inference runtime, 3) create a low-latency egress-proxy pattern as fallback, 4) autoscaler policy: max-unready 1, scale-up-cooldown 30s, scale-down-delay 300s, label burst pool as burst=true.
sara: thanks. I'll draft the quota request and spike a proxy PoC. can someone estimate cost for 3 static IPs + small proxy VMs?
kai: rough: 3 static GCP IPs ~$12/mo each; 2 n2-standard-4 proxies ~ $140/mo each pre-commit. So ~300/mo plus NAT egress charges. Spots for GPUs still dominate savings.
lisa: tagging: @arnold-sre can help with the termination-handler rollout and test infra. @ben can you pair on autoscaler tuning?
bot deploy-bot: Reminder: scheduled maintenance window `prod-gpu-pools` tomorrow 02:00-04:00 UTC. Changes during maintenance may affect new pool provisioning. :warning:
sara: noted. we'll avoid cutting the quota request during that window. thanks all :pray:
